Then \(p = q = (x - 1)^2\), so \(\sqrt{p(x)} - \sqrt{q(x)} = 0\) and the limit is \(0\).

solution: For H.P. the reciprocals are in A.P.: \(\frac{2}{\sin\theta}=\frac{1}{\sin(\theta-\alpha)}+\frac{1}{\sin(\theta+\alpha)}=\frac{\sin(\theta+\alpha)+\sin(\theta-\alpha)}{\sin(\theta-\alpha)\sin(\theta+\alpha)}\). Using \(\sin(\theta+\alpha)+\sin(\theta-\alpha)=2\sin\theta\cos\alpha\) and \(\sin(\theta-\alpha)\sin(\theta+\alpha)=\sin^2\theta-\sin^2\alpha\): \(\sin^2\theta-\sin^2\alpha=\sin^2\theta\cos\alpha\). So \(\sin^2\theta(1-\cos\alpha)=\sin^2\alpha=(1-\cos\alpha)(1+\cos\alpha)\), giving \(\sin^2\theta=1+\cos\alpha\) and \(\cos^2\theta=-\cos\alpha=1-2\cos^2\frac{\alpha}{2}\). Matches option A.

Since \(mv=qBR\) and \(mvR=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}\Rightarrow vR=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi m}\). Thus \(E=\dfrac{1}{2}qB\,vR=\dfrac{1}{2}qB\cdot\dfrac{nh}{2\pi m}=\dfrac{nqBh}{4\pi m}\).
